blue-lotus.note: A sacred water lily, picked by hand from our family lakes. Traditionally sipped for calm, gentle mood and dreamy sleep.

white-lotus.note: The softer, more introspective sister of the blue lotus. Enjoyed for quiet, clear calm.

hibiscus.note: Tart, ruby-red calyx and petals, rich in natural plant pigments. A cooling, refreshing cup hot or iced.

butterfly-pea.note: A deep blue flower used in Ayurveda, prized for its colour and antioxidant plant compounds.

lavender.note: Soft floral herb traditionally used to settle the mind and ease into rest.

chamomile.note: Delicate golden flowers with an apple-like sweetness. A classic evening herb.

calendula.note: Sunny marigold petals long used in balms and teas for their soothing nature.

rose.note: Fragrant petals that bring sweetness and a gentle, heart-opening note.

saffron.note: Hand-gathered threads of the crocus flower, treasured in beauty rituals for radiance.

ylang-ylang.note: A rich, sweet tropical flower that gives perfume its depth.

geranium.note: Egyptian rose geranium: green, floral and balancing.

damiana.note: A fragrant Central American leaf traditionally enjoyed for a relaxed, uplifted mood.

mullein.note: Soft, fluffy leaves traditionally used to support the lungs and as a smooth base for herbal blends.

moringa.note: The "miracle tree": tender leaves naturally rich in vitamins, minerals and antioxidants.

soursop.note: Glossy leaves of the graviola tree with gentle citrus notes, a traditional tea herb.

nettle.note: A mineral-rich green, long used as a nourishing everyday tonic.

skullcap.note: A gentle nervine herb traditionally used to soften tension.

lemon-balm.note: A bright, lemony mint traditionally used to lift the mood and calm nerves.

peppermint.note: Cool and clearing, an ancient herb of the Egyptians and Romans.

mugwort.note: An old dreaming herb, earthy and slightly bitter.

wild-dagga.note: Bright orange flowers from South Africa, traditionally smoked for a relaxed, uplifted mood.

white-sage.note: A sacred cleansing herb, burned with reverence for the peoples who carry its tradition.

black-sage.note: Earthy, sweet and musky, used for deep cleansing and dreamwork.

rosemary.note: Traditionally used in hair rituals for an invigorated scalp.

lemongrass.note: Zesty grass with a clean citrus scent.

black-tea.note: Bold Sri Lankan black tea. Naturally contains caffeine.

valerian.note: An earthy root traditionally taken in the evening for deep rest.

dandelion.note: A gently bitter root traditionally used to support digestion and the liver.

milk-thistle.note: Seeds traditionally used to support the liver.

marshmallow.note: A soft, soothing root traditionally used for the throat and gut.

turmeric.note: Golden Ceylon root, warming and traditionally used for balance and digestion.

ginger.note: A warming, spicy root that brightens every blend.

cinnamon.note: True cinnamon from Sri Lanka: sweet, delicate and warming.

cardamom.note: Fragrant green pods, the soul of a masala chai.

clove.note: Intensely warming flower buds, used in Ayurveda for balance.

fennel.note: Sweet seeds traditionally taken after meals to ease digestion.

allspice.note: Berries that taste of clove, nutmeg and cinnamon at once.

black-pepper.note: A pinch of heat that helps turmeric do its work.

black-seed.note: A revered seed in Middle Eastern and South Asian hair and skin oils.

annatto.note: Brick-red seeds that lend balms their warm golden colour.

elderberry.note: Dark berries traditionally simmered into syrup for the colder months.

lime.note: Tangy, dried lime for a bright finish.

reishi.note: The mushroom of immortality, rich in antioxidants.

cacao.note: Pure Peruvian cacao butter, rich in fatty acids, that melts at skin temperature.

cacao-bean.note: 100% pure, full-bean cacao from the Bribri people of Costa Rica.

frankincense.note: A sacred tree resin with a bright, resinous smoke, used in ritual for thousands of years.

dragons-blood.note: A deep red plant resin, burned for protection.

palo-santo.note: Holy wood from South America, gathered only after the tree has fallen naturally.

lilac.note: Floral notes blended into the resin.

almond-oil.note: A light, nourishing oil that carries the herbs into the skin.

tallow.note: Organic grass-fed beef tallow, one of the most skin-compatible moisturisers there is.

beeswax.note: Gives balms their soft, whipped body.

magnesium.note: A mineral that soaks in through the skin, traditionally used to relax muscles.

oat-straw.note: A nourishing, mineral-rich green stem traditionally used to steady the nerves.
